purpose: Blind adversarial reading packet. It contains the candidate and primary-source chain, but not the author's verdict or the registered prediction.

candidate.taskSketch: Repair a crash-safe publisher that creates a commit from staged content and advances a verifier-owned remote ref. A crash may occur after the remote accepted the update but before the publisher recorded completion. The publisher's protocol can read the current remote ref and submit a compare-and-swap update, but Git does not expose the remote repository's reflog to clients.
candidate.value: the exact new commit object ID and expected old remote object ID used by the first reference update
candidate.committedEvidence: a durable local publish-intent record written before the remote update, containing both object IDs
candidate.boundary: publisher crash after the remote reference transaction commits but before its acknowledgement is recorded locally
candidate.recomputation: rebuild the commit from the same tree and message using the new committer time, then read the now-current remote ref and use both recomputed values for another compare-and-swap update
candidate.movedInput: the commit's committer timestamp and the remote branch tip
candidate.localCheckOutcome: the second update succeeds and the checked-out tree matches the intended content
candidate.gradedOn: the verifier-owned remote reflog and object graph, which reveal two successful updates and two commit object IDs for one publish action
candidate.whyUnreadable: Git's documented remote-tracking refs expose only the last-known remote tip, and its documented reflogs are local and not shared with remotes; the subject has the Git transport, not filesystem access to the verifier-owned bare repository

unreachableBoundary.what: the remote repository's reflog and server-side object history
unreachableBoundary.enforcedBy: a separate verifier-owned Git server/process whose transport exposes ref tips and update results but not its local reflog

relevantSections: DESCRIPTION: an update can verify an expected old object ID before storing a new object ID
TRANSACTIONS: refs are locked against matching old IDs and modifications commit together
LOGGING UPDATES: each reflog entry records old and new object IDs
OBJECTS: an object ID hashes its type and contents; commit contents include committer time
REFERENCES: branches are mutable names for commit IDs; remote-tracking refs are last-known remote state
REFLOGS: reflogs record local ref changes and are not shared with remotes

readerQuestions: Does a real boundary prevent the subject from reading the grading witness, or is the claimed boundary only an assumption about what it will inspect?
Is the original value recoverable from evidence committed before the boundary?
Is recomputation a natural implementation move, and can it silently yield a different value?
Can ordinary subject-authored tests using the shipped interface witness the divergence?
Does the candidate reduce to an existing registered family or mechanism closely enough that it is not a new discovery under data/phase-11-preregistration.json?
Which of the nine screens should reject it first, if any?
